$comment: Shared-patch baseline (U-L3-01). Read by script/check-shared-patches.ts and script/check-opencode-annotations.ts. Each shared upstream file that Kilo adds or changes needs an entry: rung (3 = seam patch, 4 = feature patch) and the missing seam. `unmarked` allows lines without markers and states why. Raise a limit only in the PR that adds the patch, and lower it when a patch goes away.

packages/cli/src/run/noninteractive.ts.seam: `run --auto` replies `once` to every permission request. A request whose metadata sets `interactive: true` is rejected instead, so a headless run cannot approve it. The Kilo sandbox asks `sandbox_escalation` with that flag before a Git command runs outside the sandbox. No plugin hook reaches the CLI's permission replies (the permission domain has only `evaluate`), and the host does not own the non-interactive run loop. Upstream never sets the flag, so its behavior does not change.

packages/core/src/tool-output.ts.seam: Export the existing layer and cleanup node so the Kilo host can decorate native file allocations while preserving native truncation and cleanup. A plugin cannot observe allocation provenance, and replacing the service without these exports would duplicate the upstream implementation. No algorithm or upstream default changes.

specs/v2/session-sync.md.seam: Repository-specific native session sync design and operator commands. The v2 specification directory holds the producer contract; the cloud repository holds service admission, storage, and rollout. This contract now states canonical workspace-root routing, restored/reconnected ownership, bounded pending admission and credential/account fences (+13 non-empty marked lines), and paged model discovery (+3). The exact 16-line documentation growth raises only the markedLines budget from 1660 to 1676; file, unmarked-line and deletion budgets are unchanged. Plugin hooks and host composition cannot supply repository specification text. Runtime and RPC implementations remain in Kilo-owned paths; this shared-file growth is documentation only.

packages/cli/src/commands/commands.ts.seam: Optional full-TUI --model/-m argument, passed to the existing TUI Args.model selector. The CLI command specification is closed and has no host extension for root parameters; no default changes when omitted. Two generic lines across the root specification and default handler replace a custom argument parser or a second host command mirror.

packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/defau.seam: Pass the optional model flag into the existing TUI Args.model input. The root handler's private run() options cannot be supplied by the server host or a TUI plugin. Omitted input preserves the upstream behavior.

.github/actions/setup-bun/action.yml.seam: Windows CI setup: exclude the workspace, temp and Bun directories from Defender real-time scanning before the install. Carried over from v1 (`main`). The Windows Bun cache skip that Kilo also carried is upstream since v2.0.31 (anomalyco/opencode#55866). No seam: the composite action has no input to run a step before the install, and every job that installs dependencies uses it. Also pins `actions/setup-node` (v7.1.0) and `actions/cache` (v6.1.0) to current releases; upstream's pins lag and an action reference cannot be overridden from outside the composite action. Pull requests restore the newest Bun cache for the same OS, CPU and Bun version (they never save it), and the install stops an attempt after ten minutes and retries up to three times, because `bun install` has no network timeout and a stalled download held a job for its full hour.

.github/actions/setup-git-committer/acti.seam: CI authentication: pin `actions/create-github-app-token` to the current release (v3.3.0) so Kilo CI uses a supported action. Upstream's pin lags, and an action reference cannot be overridden from outside the composite action.

.github/workflows/check.yml.seam: CI triggers and gates: run `check` on push to Kilo's `v2` integration branch (upstream's v2 line is `dev`) and for every pull request, so stacked v2 PRs that target another PR branch are checked; skip `lint:changed` on upstream sync PRs (branch `sync-v*`), whose changed files are upstream's and fail upstream's lint too. No seam: workflow triggers and step conditions cannot be extended from outside the file. Also pins `actions/checkout` (v7.0.1) to the current release; upstream's pin lags.

.github/workflows/check-test.yml.seam: Upstream renamed `test.yml` to `check-test.yml` in v2.2. CI triggers: run the unit and e2e matrix on push to Kilo's `v2` integration branch (upstream's v2 line is `dev`). Skip the `affected` job, and with it the `e2e-suite` jobs that need it and the `e2e` result check that requires `affected` to succeed: they test only `packages/app` and `packages/session-ui`, which Kilo removed (`skipFiles` in script/upstream/utils/config.ts). Job-level lines, so upstream changes to the e2e steps still merge cleanly. `Build workspace libraries` in upstream's `build` job filters only on `@opencode/cli^...`, because turbo fails on the `@opencode/app^...` filter when the package does not exist. CI speed: `Verify packed workerd SDK` runs in its own `sdk` job (at the end of the file), so it no longer waits for the unit tests in `unit`. The Turbo cache step (upstream removed its broken one in v2.0.31) uses `.turbo/cache` (where Turborepo 2.x writes), keys on turbo.json and bun.lock, and carries the shard. Test shards: a `shard` matrix dimension in `unit` (2 Linux, 4 Windows) sets `KILO_TEST_SHARD` and `KILO_TEST_CONCURRENCY`; core, tui and cli run `test:ci` (the Kilo runner, script/kilocode/test/test-runner.ts) at turbo concurrency 3, and the `packages` leg runs the other packages with `test` alongside the Kilo host suite: that suite uses `test:ci` unsplit at concurrency 4 because its one heavy file would be a long pole inside a shard job; failing cases from the runner's JUnit reports become annotations, and the reports are an artifact from every leg that refreshes the shard weights. No seam: workflow triggers, job conditions, jobs, steps, matrix dimensions and cache keys cannot be extended from outside the file. Upstream has no cache key input or test shard option. Action pins track current releases (`actions/checkout` v7.0.1, `actions/setup-node` v7.1.0, `actions/cache` v6.1.0, `actions/upload-artifact` v7.0.2, `mikepenz/action-junit-report` v6.6.1) and the generated protocol client is checked next to the generated client. Required-check barriers: `unit-required` (name `unit (linux)`) and `required` (name `test (linux)`) aggregate the `unit` matrix, `build` and `sdk`, so a branch ruleset has stable check names; a draft pull request and a quarantine dispatch skip the matrix and the build on purpose, so both barriers accept `skipped` for exactly those two cases and still fail on any other skip; `--affected` now applies to pull requests only, so pushes and manual runs test the full suite; `test:lint-rules` runs next to the Effect rule tests. No seam: a matrix job cannot publish one stable check name, a ruleset cannot require a job that does not exist, and the test invocation is a run step inside the job.

.gitignore.seam: Ignore the v1 line's local dev profile (`.kilo-dev/`, left behind when one checkout switches between `main` and `v2`), `telemetry-id`, generated dependency installs, merge reports, and JetBrains state under `.kilo/`, and `packages/app/.artifacts/`. No seam: root gitignore rules cannot live in a Kilo-owned file. The v2 `bun dev` profile moved into the Kilo host package (packages/kilo-cli/.gitignore, U-E0-01); the remaining patterns are not host entries and stay. Reconciled by 3-way merge during upstream syncs.
.gitignore.unmarked: Eleven ignore patterns. A gitignore pattern line cannot carry an inline comment, so each pattern is preceded by a `# kilocode_change:` comment line.

.oxlintrc.json.seam: Oxlint loads one repository config and has no host-level rule composition, so the Kilo VS Code size and complexity overrides must live in the shared root config.

.github/pull_request_template.md.seam: Remove upstream's `### Visual` animated SVG section (`packages/desktop` beta dialog, skipped by Kilo in `script/upstream/utils/config.ts`), which GitHub renders as raw XML and which caused agents and contributors to paste unrendered wireframe SVGs into PR bodies. No seam: GitHub reads a single root `.github/pull_request_template.md`.

AGENTS.md.seam: One marked block at the top with the Kilo rules for the v2 line (integration branch `origin/v2`, moving base, branch names, `bun dev` isolation instead of `dev:live`, plugin-first placement, direction of code movement, checks, read `migration-tracking/principles.md` first), pointing at the plan, the principles, issue #15297 and the skills, plus requiring localization: every Kilo UI string ships with its key in all `packages/kilo-i18n/src` locales (upstream's "English source strings only" rule applies to upstream copy only). It also replaces the upstream desktop-beta `### Visual` animated SVG rule under Commits and PR Titles with Kilo `## Proof` verification (screenshots/recordings or real `bun dev` run output). It overrides the upstream rules it contradicts (default branch `dev`, `dev:live` against the installed service). Instructions only, no behavior. No seam: `AGENTS.md` is the only root instruction file that every agent used on this repository reads (v2 core loads only `AGENTS.md`, `core/src/config/plugin/instruction.ts`). A Kilo `instructions` entry in a root `kilo.json` would reach Kilo sessions only, and the contradicting upstream rules would still be in this file.

CONTRIBUTING.md.seam: Development setup names the exact Bun version from `packageManager` (3 lines). Documentation for contributors of this repository; `bun run build` and `install:alpha` fail on another Bun version. No seam: the contributor guide is a single upstream-owned file and has no Kilo-owned equivalent that GitHub shows. Goes away when the Kilo docs replace CONTRIBUTING.md.

README.md.seam: Show the generated Kilo v2 migration progress map (badge, treemap, history from migration-tracking/progress/) on the branch front page. Visibility only, no behavior. No seam: the repository README is a single upstream-owned file, and a Kilo-owned README cannot be the front page of the same repository. The Kilo host (U-E0-01) is a package and does not change the front page. Goes away when the map is published outside the repository (for example GitHub Pages).

package.json.seam: Root `dev` script runs script/dev-isolated.ts, which starts the Kilo host entry (packages/kilo-cli) with an isolated profile, so `bun dev` never uses the installed OpenCode or Kilo data. Stays after U-E0-01: `bun dev` from the root reads the upstream root package.json, and upstream's script runs the upstream CLI with the real data. Root `extension` script runs packages/kilo-vscode/script/launch.ts (Kilo-owned), which builds the v2 VS Code extension and opens it in a separate VS Code instance with an isolated profile, as `bun run extension` does on v1. Root `lint` script runs only `oxlint`: its ast-grep and `script/sdk-docs.ts` steps check upstream's GUI plugin package (`packages/gui-extensions`, renamed to `packages/gui-plugins` in v2.2), which Kilo removed (`skipFiles`). Root `install:alpha` script runs script/kilocode/install-alpha.ts (Kilo-owned), which installs the host executable built by the `kilo-v2` workflow; it goes away when v2 is mainline. Root devDependency `@types/node` (catalog version): TypeScript searches `node_modules/@types` in every parent directory before it follows a package's own dependencies, and Agent Manager worktrees live inside another checkout (`.kilo/worktrees/<name>`). Without a root copy, packages that do not declare `@types/node` (ai, cli, tui, server and others) load the parent checkout's version, so a worktree's typecheck depends on what another checkout installed. No lower rung: the root manifest decides what the root `node_modules/@types` contains, and `bunfig.toml` and the package tsconfigs are upstream files too. `patchedDependencies` registers `patches/virtua@0.49.1.patch` (Kilo-owned, the same patch as v1), which adds `VirtualizerHandle.measure()` and clamps the rendered range to the data length; the v2 VS Code transcript (packages/kilo-vscode/webview-ui/src/v2/messages.tsx) uses `measure()` to re-pin the bottom when the live turn is handed to the virtualizer. No seam: bun reads patches only from the root package.json. `overrides` raises `@xmldom/xmldom` to the patched 0.9 line for the DOCX reader, and `patchedDependencies` registers `patches/mammoth@1.12.0.patch`, which adapts mammoth to the 0.9 API. Both are the v1 dependency decisions; bun reads overrides and patches only from the root manifest.

packages/cli/package.json.seam: Export `./*` (`./src/*.ts`) as `core`, `server` and `util` do, so the Kilo host (packages/kilo-cli, U-E0-01) can run the upstream command handlers and services. Generic: any embedding entry can use it. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot supply it: the CLI exported only `./run` and `./server-process`, so no entry outside the package could reach `Commands`, `Runtime` or a handler. Add a `test:ci` script that runs the Kilo test runner (script/kilocode/test/test-runner.ts) in balanced shards for CI. Turborepo runs only package.json scripts, so the sharded task needs a script in each sharded package (core, tui, cli); the package's own `test` script stays as it is and the runner calls it with file arguments.

packages/cli/script/app-assets.ts.seam: Build an empty web UI archive when `packages/app` does not exist, because Kilo removed it (`skipFiles` in script/upstream/utils/config.ts). One generic condition covers the release build (`build.ts`) and the Node build (`build-node.ts`). The server then answers non-API paths with 404, as on v1. No seam: the build scripts call `buildAppArchive` directly.

packages/cli/script/service-smoke.ts.seam: Accept a 404 for the web UI shell in the compiled service smoke test, because the Kilo build embeds no web UI (`packages/app` removed). The API, authentication, and plugin checks still run. No seam: the smoke script has no option to skip the web UI check.

packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/mcp/a.seam: Kilo config write target for `mcp add` (feature `config`): the first existing file of `.kilo2/kilo2.jsonc`, `.kilo2/kilo2.json`, `kilo2.jsonc`, `kilo2.json`, else `kilo2.json`; the global directory checks only its root files. Internal releases use kilo2 names without a v1 fallback (decision 12); the file order follows v1. Rung 4: the handler imports a Kilo module (util/src/kilocode/config/files.ts, which holds the names and order) and calls out to it. No seam: the CLI never builds Core `Config` and may not import Core (`test/import-boundaries.test.ts`), so the discovery layout node does not reach it, and Kilo's write order (directory before root files, `.jsonc` first, global root-only) differs in shape from upstream's, so a generic knob would be Kilo-shaped. The call-out is unconditional, so the upstream `packages/cli` binary (not shipped) also writes `kilo2.json` while its server reads only `opencode.*`.

packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/plugi.seam: Kilo config path for `plugin add` and `plugin remove` (feature `config`): pass global mode to `resolveConfigPath` (mcp/add.ts) so the global directory checks only its root files, like Kilo v1. Rung 4: one marked line each; the order lives in util/src/kilocode/config/files.ts. No hook, node or option for the config path in the CLI handlers.

Kilo config path for `plugin add` and `plugin remove` (feature `config`): pass global mode to `resolveConfigPath` (mcp/add.ts) so the global directory checks only its root files, like Kilo v1. Rung 4: one marked line each; the order lives in util/src/kilocode/config/files.ts. No hook, node or option for the config path in the CLI handlers.

packages/cli/src/server-process.ts.seam: `Options.overrides` (service replacements), passed through to `ServerProcess.start` in packages/server/src/process.ts, so an embedding entry's `serve` handler can replace services in the server it starts. The Kilo host registers the Kilo plugins this way (`SdkPlugins.node` replacement, U-E0-01). Two lines, no Kilo value. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot supply it: `run` built the server options itself and had no way to add a replacement.

packages/client/src/promise/generated/ty.seam: Generated client types for schema additions Kilo exposes: the optional command template and model metadata on the command list API, and the optional PTY create size. The client must be regenerated from the public schema. It also carries the optional `steer` query parameter of `session.interrupt`.
packages/client/src/promise/generated/ty.unmarked: Generated TypeScript cannot retain manual marker comments; bun run generate owns this file.

packages/protocol/openapi.json.seam: Generated OpenAPI document for the optional command template and model metadata exposed by the command list API, the optional PTY create size exposed by packages/schema/src/pty.ts, and the `hook` action variant of `Schedule.Action` that lets Kilo-owned Flows own a schedule row without admitting a native prompt. The document is generated from the public schema; editing it by hand is not supported. It also documents the optional `steer` query parameter of `session.interrupt` and the `interrupted: false` outcome it can produce.
packages/protocol/openapi.json.unmarked: Generated JSON cannot carry marker comments; bun run generate in packages/protocol owns this file.

packages/core/package.json.seam: Add a `test:ci` script that runs the Kilo test runner (script/kilocode/test/test-runner.ts) in balanced shards for CI. Turborepo runs only package.json scripts, so the sharded task needs a script in each sharded package (core, tui, cli); the package's own `test` script stays as it is and the runner calls it with file arguments.

packages/core/src/config.ts.seam: Config discovery layout (feature `config`): `ConfigDiscovery.LayoutService`, a global node with upstream defaults (`opencode.json`, `opencode.jsonc`, `.opencode`, no walk bound) that discovery and `Config` read for the root file names, the project directory names, the file order inside those directories, the upward-walk bound and the global write target (the last existing name). Optional systemFiles and parse hooks let a host select managed file order and decode its own config schema from raw and normalized fields; the decoder also preserves host fields when managed policies split from settings. Optional input normalization and command document composition let the host apply model-only overrides after file discovery. Upstream's integration reloads (v2.2) run discovery with a captured layer context, so that context also carries the layout service. Without the hooks, the default graph and canonical schema behave as upstream. The Kilo host supplies kilo2 names, file orders, a worktree boundary and Kilo-owned config policy. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot do it alone: config parsing precedes plugins, the command editor cannot update captured definitions, and replacing Config.node would lose the server's configured options. Codebase indexing (feature `indexing`): an optional `reload` re-reads the config sources after a host write, so a saved `indexing` key applies also when `fs.filewatcher` is false. It runs the same reload as the watcher and publishes `config.updated` when the result changes. Without a caller nothing changes. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot do it: the reload is a closure inside the Config layer.

packages/core/src/schedule.ts.seam: Generic due-schedule claim seam for location plugins. An experimental session hook receives a due time schedule before native prompt admission; claiming it suppresses that prompt while preserving the scheduler's existing leader election, advancement, retry and outcome bookkeeping. A hook-owned action remains suppressed when its owner is unavailable and rejects native conditions that could otherwise admit it. Schedule.create accepts an internal optional requireEnabled flag so a host plugin can own a backing schedule without enabling OpenCode's native schedule UI; the default remains true. The hook runs before the native experimental.schedules check, and only unclaimed occurrences honor that flag, so a plugin-owned schedule keeps firing while the native UI is disabled; a hook failure leaves the row unclaimed and uses the existing failed-retry backoff. Kilo managed Flows use the hook and option, but no Kilo value lives here. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot reach the scheduler between its due-time claim and prompt admission, and a second plugin-owned timing loop would duplicate leader election and advancement behavior.

packages/schema/src/schedule.ts.seam: Add a generic hook-owned schedule action alongside the native prompt action. The scheduler advances it without native prompt admission even when its plugin owner is unavailable, while the public schedule-create request remains prompt-only. A plugin hook cannot make the stored action safe before plugin activation, and host composition cannot persist ownership in the shared schedule model.

packages/core/src/config/discovery.ts.seam: Config discovery layout (feature `config`): `ConfigDiscovery.LayoutService` supplies names, discovery, parsing and optional managed directories with upstream defaults. Optional input normalization and command document composition let a host validate extensions and apply overrides after command discovery. Without these hooks the upstream behavior is unchanged; a caller that does not provide the layout node (upstream discovery tests) gets the upstream defaults. The Kilo host supplies kilo2 paths and Kilo-owned policy. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot reach native normalization or update captured command definitions, and replacing Config.node would lose the server's configured options.

packages/core/src/command.ts.seam: Keep optional template and model metadata on registered commands and return it from command.list. The command editor exposes only add and cannot recover a definition's captured config after registration. Definitions without metadata remain unchanged.

packages/core/src/ripgrep.ts.seam: Accept ripgrep's base64 `bytes` shape alongside `text` for the matched path, line and submatch. Ripgrep emits `bytes` as soon as one byte of a record is not valid UTF-8, and the text-only schema then rejected the record and failed the whole search with `Invalid ripgrep match output`. Bytes decode as lossy UTF-8 with the replacement character, and the line and submatch limits still apply after decoding. No plugin hook or host composition reaches this parser: it runs inside the core ripgrep service before any tool result exists, and no knob can express an alternate decoder for the fixed `rg --json` shape. Records that carry `text` behave exactly as before.

packages/core/src/config/plugin/command..seam: Compose the ordered command documents through the optional host callback after file discovery, and pass the resulting template and model to command metadata; the seam itself is rung 3. Rung 4: each prompt an expanded config command admits carries the Kilo `injected-prompt` label from `core/src/kilocode/session/injected.ts`, so a transcript can show `/name args` instead of the template the model receives. The command editor offers only `add`, a definition's `execute` builds its own prompt, and the invocation carries no metadata channel, so no plugin hook reaches these two prompt calls. The label is UI metadata only: text, delivery, the subagent prefix and every upstream default are unchanged. The command editor cannot update a captured model, and the host cannot replace Config.node without losing server-specific options. The default callback is absent and native command behavior is unchanged.

packages/core/src/plugin/command.ts.seam: Each prompt an expanded built-in command admits (`init`, `review`, an MCP prompt) carries the Kilo `injected-prompt` label from `core/src/kilocode/session/injected.ts`, so a transcript can show `/name args` instead of the template the model receives. Rungs 1 to 3 do not work: the built-in command definitions register through a command editor that offers only `add`, each definition builds its own prompt, and the invocation carries no metadata channel, so no plugin hook or pass-through parameter reaches the prompt call. The label is UI metadata only: prompt text, delivery and every upstream default are unchanged, and the plugin's upstream test observes the same prompt fields.

packages/plugin/src/effect/command.ts.seam: Allow command definitions to expose optional template and model metadata to command.list. The plugin editor otherwise discards this information; definitions without these fields retain the upstream behavior.

packages/plugin/src/promise/command.ts.seam: Mirror the optional command template and model metadata in the promise plugin interface. Existing plugin commands may omit both fields.

packages/schema/src/command.ts.seam: Expose optional template and model metadata in the command list response so clients can identify configurable commands and show their effective values. Existing commands may omit both fields.

packages/schema/src/file-diff.ts.seam: Optional `moved` flag on a file diff so clients can label a rename. The patch tool output is this shared struct and no plugin can add a field to an upstream schema; without the flag both clients report a rename as an unlabelled modification. Every other producer omits it, so upstream behavior and defaults are unchanged.

packages/core/src/mcp/host.ts.seam: Generic MCP embedding hooks (`fetch`, `localCommand`, OAuth client identity) for an embedding host. No plugin hook reaches the MCP transport or OAuth registration, and the Kilo host supplies the values through `Mcp.configured({ host })`. With `host` unset, upstream behavior and defaults are unchanged. The file carries no Kilo value.

packages/core/src/mcp/client.ts.seam: Apply the optional host `fetch` wrapper to the remote transport and the host `localCommand` rewrite to a local server command. No plugin hook reaches the MCP transport or the spawn command; the host sets both through `Mcp.configured`. Omitting the hooks preserves upstream behavior.

packages/core/src/mcp/connection.ts.seam: Carry the optional `McpHost.Host` from a connection's input to `McpClient.connect`, so the host `fetch` and `localCommand` hooks also reach connections the connection service and the pool open rather than only a direct client connect. No plugin hook reaches the MCP transport or spawn command; with `host` unset nothing changes.

packages/core/src/mcp/pool.ts.seam: Pass the process-wide `McpHost.Host` into a shared connection's `McpConnection.make`, since the pool opens shared connections from data it takes from the first holder. The host is identical for every Location in a process, so it stays out of the pool key. With `host` unset nothing changes.

packages/core/src/mcp/index.ts.seam: Carry the optional `Mcp.Options.host` embedding hooks to the client and OAuth paths. The MCP service has no plugin hook for its transport, command or OAuth identity; the host composes them through `Mcp.configured`. The construction-only field is not decoded, and an absent host changes nothing.

packages/core/src/mcp/oauth.ts.seam: Use the optional host OAuth client identity for `client_name`, `client_uri` and the initialize challenge, and let the host name the CIMD document URL. No plugin hook reaches OAuth registration; the host supplies the values through `Mcp.configured`. Defaults stay `opencode` and the upstream document.

packages/core/src/tool/mcp.ts.seam: Mark every MCP tool registration with `mcp: true`. The sandbox plugin must treat an MCP tool as delegated network authority even when a server named `opencode` exposes a tool named like a built-in, and namespace plus declared name cannot separate the two. Provenance exists only at registration and no plugin hook observes it. Without the sandbox plugin nothing reads the flag, so upstream behavior and defaults are unchanged.

packages/core/src/tool/plugin/patch.ts.seam: Set the optional `moved` flag when an update hunk has a move target. The move already applies here; only the result metadata loses the fact that it was a rename. The tool has no plugin hook for its own result metadata, and add, delete and plain update hunks stay unchanged.

packages/core/src/tool/plugin/shell.ts.seam: Two additions for the tool card. (1) Publish the running command's current output and running state while it executes. The shell tool exposes no progress stream for its own execution, and a plugin can wrap the whole execute but cannot read the shell output that execute owns. The marked block pages the shell's file-backed output on a short interval, publishes progress metadata, and stops before the call settles. (2) Add the optional `description` input the model fills with a 5-10 word summary, as the first property so models write it before the command and the card can show it while the command streams, then copy it to `metadata.description` and to the background completion notice. Upstream has no title channel on a tool result, so the card shows the raw first command line, which Kilo sessions fill with a `cd <worktree> &&` prefix that identifies nothing. Both additions are optional: omitted input, every upstream default, and the rest of the result and metadata are unchanged.

packages/core/src/tool/plugin/schedule.t.seam: The `/schedule` command's prompt carries the Kilo `injected-prompt` label from `core/src/kilocode/session/injected.ts`, so a transcript can show `/schedule <request>` instead of the expanded template the model receives. The command registers through an editor that offers only `add`, its `execute` builds its own prompt, and the invocation carries no metadata channel, so no plugin hook reaches the prompt call. The label is UI metadata only: prompt text, delivery and every upstream default are unchanged.

packages/core/test/tool-shell.test.ts.seam: Test coverage for the marked live-output progress behavior and for the optional model description. The existing progress test asserted a single update, which the new behavior supersedes; the added tests cover streamed output before exit, the bounded large-output preview, the background running state and interruption, plus that the description reaches result metadata and stays absent when omitted. The harness must stay next to the upstream shell tests because it composes the real Job, Session and Shell services.

packages/core/src/plugin/sdk.ts.seam: Registration phase for embedder plugins: `register(plugin, { phase: "post" })` and `all(phase)`. Without a phase, `all()` returns what it returned before. The Kilo agents use it: the agent ceiling must run after `ConfigAgentPlugin`, which is an internal post plugin (U-E2-12). Six lines, no Kilo value. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot supply it: the store had no phase, so every embedder plugin ran before the internal post plugins and a plugin could not act on the result of config.

packages/core/src/plugin/internal.ts.seam: Expose the existing Location-service provider to embedder plugins. The supervisor applies it without changing pre/post order or upstream defaults. Required for account config and managed policy reads at plugin activation; the public plugin context has no config domain, and host-global registration cannot supply a Location-scoped Config service. All feature logic stays in Kilo-owned plugins.

packages/core/src/plugin/supervisor.ts.seam: Appends the embedder plugins registered with phase `post` (`SdkPlugins.all("post")`) after the internal post plugins, so they see the result of config. Each activation builds a new list, because `internal.post` is shared across reloads. Provides the existing Location-service context to embedder plugins in both phases, as internal plugins already receive it. No boot-order or upstream default change. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot supply it: the supervisor builds the boot order itself, and host-global registration cannot supply Location-scoped services such as Config.

packages/client/src/promise/generated/cl.seam: Generated promise client operations for the optional PTY create size exposed by packages/schema/src/pty.ts. The client must be regenerated from the public schema. It also carries the optional `steer` query parameter of `session.interrupt`.
packages/client/src/promise/generated/cl.unmarked: Generated TypeScript cannot retain manual marker comments; bun run generate owns this file.

packages/core/src/tool/read-filesystem.t.seam: Generic ReaderError (a resource, a caller-supplied message and that message as .message) in the ReadError union, so a host-provided reader implementation can report why it could not extract a file. The reader service is the rung-2 replacement; this is only the typed failure it needs because the read tool passes known errors through and maps every other error to a bare "Unable to read <path>". No Kilo path, identifier, value or default; without a reader that raises it, upstream behavior is identical.

packages/core/src/tool/plugin/read.ts.seam: One condition in the existing typed-message list so the generic ReadToolFileSystem.ReaderError reaches the model instead of the fallback message. The read tool, its schema, codemode setting, bounding and instruction loading are unchanged; no Kilo identifier or value.

patches/mammoth@1.12.0.patch.seam: Mammoth 1.12.0 is written for the @xmldom/xmldom 0.8 errorHandler API. Kilo raises xmldom to the patched 0.9 line for the XML injection and resource-consumption fixes, so mammoth's xml reader must use the 0.9 onError API and pass text/xml. Set through patchedDependencies in the root package.json, so the patch applies from the root install. The same patch and override ship on v1. No lower rung: the parser call is inside mammoth's shipped lib/xml/xmldom.js and no host or plugin hook replaces that module.
patches/mammoth@1.12.0.patch.unmarked: A patch file is applied verbatim; a marker inside the diff would change the patched source. The same patch ships on v1.

packages/patchmark/test/slow-inputs.test.seam: Kilo CI stability: the 1 MB one-char-at-a-time streaming test keeps its deterministic scan-work assertion, but the wall-clock timeout in the same test is upstream's default, and Windows CI runners crossed it at ~18 s against a 15 s ceiling. The input is reduced to 256 KB, which keeps the identical constant-work-per-character bound, and the timeout is raised to 60 s as a guard for catastrophic regressions only. No seam: bun's per-test timeout and the payload size are inside an upstream test file, and the test suite belongs to the upstream package that Kilo cannot replace (inline patch, option 4).

packages/core/src/session.ts.seam: `Session.Interface.interrupt` accepts the optional `steer` flag and passes it to `SessionExecution`. A client that steers a running turn needs the server to tell 'stop this model call' apart from 'stop everything'; the interrupt options are the only input the execution layer reads, and no plugin hook reaches interruption. Upstream callers never set the flag, so their behavior does not change.

packages/core/src/session/execution.ts.seam: `SessionExecution.interrupt` does not stop the execution when the interruption carries `steer` and a compaction is durably running, so a steered prompt can never cancel a checkpoint. The checkpoint is all-or-nothing and its summary may already be paid for; the admitted prompt is delivered at the boundary after the compaction. An interruption without the flag still cancels one. No plugin hook reaches interruption, and upstream never sets the flag. Rung 1 cannot do this: a Kilo RPC can read the Session context and then call interrupt, but that is check-then-act across awaits, and the gap is exactly when a steer is sent, right after a response ends and automatic compaction opens. No plugin hook runs before interruption; plugins only observe it afterwards, so only the interruption itself can decide atomically. A host mirror of SessionExecution would duplicate the coordinator, the write-ahead claim and restart recovery for this one row read.

packages/core/src/session/session.ts.seam: Pass the optional `steer` flag from the Session handle to `SessionExecution.interrupt`. The handle is the only path to interruption, so no plugin seam exists. Omitted, the call is unchanged.

packages/core/test/session-execution.tes.seam: Test for the steer guard: a steer-marked interruption returns false and leaves the running compaction row alone, while the same request without the flag still interrupts. The suite belongs to the upstream package, and the case only exists for Kilo's flag.

packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts.seam: Optional `steer` query parameter on `session.interrupt`, with descriptions for it and its response, so a client can mark an interruption issued to deliver a prompt. Omitted, the endpoint behaves as upstream.

packages/server/src/handlers/session.ts.seam: Forward the `steer` query parameter to `Session.interrupt`. The handler owns the endpoint input and no plugin hook sees it; omitted, the call is unchanged.

packages/core/src/plugin.ts.seam: Plugin source resolver seam (feature `plugin`, cell plugin:25cfde80052f): `Plugin.configured(options)` decorates the registry node with a loader-options service through `mapLayer`, so an embedding host can resolve its own plugin source syntax (Kilo's `git:` specs) without the shared loader knowing about it. The node still provides `Plugin.Service`, its service, layer and dependencies keep their single upstream declaration, and the extra service changes nothing when a host does not configure it. No plugin hook reaches the loader's local/npm split before a plugin is active. Rung 3 because rung 1 has no hook before activation and rung 2 cannot replace the registry without losing the server's configured options.

packages/core/src/plugin/module.ts.seam: Plugin source resolver seam (feature `plugin`, cell plugin:25cfde80052f): `PluginModule.Options.pluginSource` lets an embedding host map a configured target to the directory the loader should read, before the existing local-path/npm split, name the `plugin.use` resources the resolution stands for (so a deny-list cannot be bypassed by another spelling), and report `pending` when the source needs the installing pass instead of the fast pass, and let the loader evaluate those resources on the read pass first so a denied plugin is blocked before the resolver reaches the network. The hook returns `undefined` for every upstream target, so npm packages and local directories behave exactly as before. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot reach the loader: the split runs inside `PluginModule.load`, after the plugin registry, and a host cannot supply the Npm or source loading steps from outside it. Kilo supplies `git:` clone resolution here.
